units.source: Calendar
units.context: Calendar

units.source: The Calendar view will display each child note in a calendar that has a start date and optionally an end date, as an event.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: The Calendar view has multiple display modes:
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Month view, where the entire month is displayed and all-day events can be inserted. Both time-specific events and all-day events are listed.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Week view, where all the 7 days of the week (or 5 if the weekends are hidden) are displayed in columns. This mode allows entering and displaying time-specific events, not just all-day events.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Day view, which views only a single day. Especially useful for heavy agendas or mobile views.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: List view, which displays all the events of a given month in sequence.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Year view, which displays the entire year for quick reference.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Unlike other Collection view types, the Calendar view also allows some kind of interaction, such as moving events around as well as creating new ones.
units.context: Calendar

units.source: Creating a calendar__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Creating a calendar

units.source: Right click on an existing note in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and select __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ → __TRILIUM_PH_4__Collection__TRILIUM_PH_5__ → __TRILIUM_PH_6__Calendar__TRILIUM_PH_7__.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a calendar

units.source: Creating a new event/note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: To create a new event:
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: First, click the desired day (month & year views) or the desired timeslot (day view).
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: Alternatively, drag across multiple days (or time slots) to set both the start and end date.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: In either cases, a small popup will show with a prompt for a title and the date & time of the event that will be created. The date and time can be changed there the same way as in the popup view of an existing event (see below).
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: At this point, the event hasn't been created yet to protect against accidental clicks. Add a title optionally and press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create__TRILIUM_PH_1__ button. If no title is provided, the event will follow the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_3__ rules.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__ template field below the date and time shows the note type or template the event's note is made from. To make the event from another one, press the field and select it from the list; the calendar remembers the choice for the next event. Select __TRILIUM_PH_1__More templates…__TRILIUM_PH_2__ to change which templates are listed (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__). The date and time entered for the event replace any dates and times the template carries.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: To give the event a time before creating it (for example, after clicking a day in the month view), press __TRILIUM_PH_0__Add time__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and set the start and end time; the duration is shown to the right of them. To make the event all-day again, press the __TRILIUM_PH_2__ button at the end of the row. Adding or removing a time keeps the dates, so an event can start at a time on one day and end at a time on another (for example, a night shift). Changing the start date or time moves the end by the same amount, keeping the duration. An empty end date means the event ends on the day it starts; setting the end time before the start time moves the end date to the next day.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: After creating the event, it will show up on the calendar. To edit the content of the event (including recurrence), click on it to bring it into the popup view.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: Creating new notes from the calendar will respect the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation if set on the Collection note.
units.context: Calendar > Creating a new event/note

units.source: Interacting with events__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: Hovering the mouse over an event will display information about the note.__TRILIUM_PH_0____TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: Left clicking the event will open a dedicated popup to quickly configure the event or edit its note content.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: Right click will offer more options including opening the note in a new split or window.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: Drag and drop an event on the calendar to move it to another day.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: The length of an event can be changed by placing the mouse to the right edge of the event and dragging the mouse around.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: On a __TRILIUM_PH_0__read-only__TRILIUM_PH_1__ calendar, events can't be dragged, resized or created, their context menu only offers the places to open them in, and the button to pin the current date is hidden. Switching between the month, week and day views still works, but the choice isn't saved.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events

units.source: Popup view__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: When an event is clicked, a popup will show near the event which contains the following inforamtion:
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: The title and icon of the event, both editable.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Buttons to interact with the event:
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Open the event in the same pane, new tab, etc.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Color picker to change the color of the event.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Button to remove the event from the calendar, which can optionally delete its corresponding note.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Calendar-specific features:
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: The start date and, for an event spanning several days, the end date.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: The start and end time with the duration to the right of them, and a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button that removes the time, making the event all-day. An all-day event shows an __TRILIUM_PH_1__Add time__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button instead.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: A full recurrence editor, opened from the dropdown below the time, to have the same event show up weekly, monthly, etc.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: The __TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the marker, if any.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: The note's content which can be edited directly from the panel.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: To dismiss the popup:
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Press the X button at the top-right of the popup.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: In the calendar, press anywhere outside the popup.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Or simply press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Escape__TRILIUM_PH_1__ key.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: It is possible to switch between events by clicking on them even when the popup view is already open.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Events can have __TRILIUM_PH_0__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_1__ between them and clicking on such a link will automatically navigate the calendar to the right date and the popup view to the new note.
units.context: Calendar > Interacting with events > Popup view

units.source: Interaction on mobile__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: When Trilium is on mobile, the interaction with the calendar is slightly different:
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: Clicking on an event displays the popup view, which allows editing the event.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: Long-presing an event triggers the contextual menu, including the option to open in __TRILIUM_PH_0__Quick edit__TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: To insert a new event, touch and hold the empty space. When successful, the empty space will become colored to indicate the selection.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: Before releasing, drag across multiple spaces to create multi-day events.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: When released, a prompt will appear to enter the note title.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: To move an existing event, touch and hold the event until the empty space near it will become colored.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: At this point the event can be dragged across other days on the calendar.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: Or the event can be resized by tapping on the small circle to the right end of the event.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: To exit out of editing mode, simply tap the empty space anywhere on the calendar.
units.context: Calendar > Interaction on mobile

units.source: Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: By default, a new event is a __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ note. To make events from other note types, or from __TRILIUM_PH_2__Templates__TRILIUM_PH_3__ with predefined content and attributes (such as a color), open the __TRILIUM_PH_4__ __TRILIUM_PH_5__Calendar properties__TRILIUM_PH_6__ dialog from the __TRILIUM_PH_7__Note menu__TRILIUM_PH_8__ or from the settings menu of the __TRILIUM_PH_9__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_10__, and find __TRILIUM_PH_11__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_12__. Here you can:
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Include a note type or note template already created in your knowledge base by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Add existing template__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button and then selecting the desired note type or template.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Create a new template by pressing the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Create a new template__TRILIUM_PH_2__ button. The template is created as a child of the calendar, and is not shown as an event.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button to remove a template from the list. The template is removed only from the list, not deleted.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Press the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ button of a custom template to edit, open in a new window, duplicate, or delete it.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Drag a template by its handle to reorder the list shown when creating an event.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: The dialog is not available on a read-only calendar, or on a calendar marked with __TRILIUM_PH_0__ or __TRILIUM_PH_1__ (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__Using with the Journal / calendar__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event templates

units.source: Event attributes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: Events can show the values of their attributes below their title, in the month view, and in the week and day views for all-day events and for timed ones tall enough to hold them. To choose which attributes are shown, open the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ __TRILIUM_PH_1__Calendar properties__TRILIUM_PH_2__ dialog (see __TRILIUM_PH_3__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_4__ for how to open it) and find __TRILIUM_PH_5__Event attributes__TRILIUM_PH_6__. It lists the __TRILIUM_PH_7__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_8__ the calendar defines, and those its events define themselves. Here you can:
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: Turn an attribute on to show it on the events. New attributes are hidden until you turn them on, which keeps the calendar from getting cluttered.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: Drag an attribute by its handle to change the order in which the events show them.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: Create a new attribute, which is shown on the events right away, or edit or delete one the calendar defines.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: The dates, times and recurrence of the events are not listed, as the calendar always shows them itself.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: To change an attribute's value without opening the event, right-click the event (or long-press it on a phone) and use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__ section of its context menu. It lists the shown attributes of the “checkbox”, “select” and “date” types, and works as on a __TRILIUM_PH_2__Kanban Board__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: If an event has a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label, including one inherited from the calendar, the attributes listed in that label are shown instead.
units.context: Calendar > Configuring the calendar view > Event attributes

units.source: How the calendar works__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > How the calendar works

units.source: The calendar displays all the child notes of the Collection that have a __TRILIUM_PH_0__. An __TRILIUM_PH_1__ can optionally be added.
units.context: Calendar > How the calendar works

units.context: Calendar > How the calendar works

units.context: Calendar > How the calendar works

units.source: When not used in a Journal, the calendar is recursive. That is, it will look for events not just in its child notes but also in the children of these child notes.

units.source: Limiting the depth__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > How the calendar works > Limiting the depth

units.source: To limit how deep the calendar looks for events, set __TRILIUM_PH_0__Maximum nesting depth__TRILIUM_PH_1__ under __TRILIUM_PH_2__Included notes__TRILIUM_PH_3__ in the __TRILIUM_PH_4____TRILIUM_PH_5__Calendar properties__TRILIUM_PH_6__ dialog (see __TRILIUM_PH_7__Event templates__TRILIUM_PH_8__ for how to open it), or the __TRILIUM_PH_9__ label: __TRILIUM_PH_10__ shows only the child notes, __TRILIUM_PH_11__ adds their children, and so on. units.source: Note that the recurrence string does not include the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute as defined in the iCAL specifications. This is derived directly from the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and __TRILIUM_PH_2__ attributes
units.context: Calendar > Recurrence > Custom recurrence using a subset of RRULE

units.source: If you want to override the label the calendar uses to fetch the recurrence string, you can use the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute. For example, you can set __TRILIUM_PH_1__. Then you can set your recurrence string like __TRILIUM_PH_2__
units.context: Calendar > Recurrence > Custom recurrence using a subset of RRULE

units.source: Also note that the recurrence label can be made promoted as with the start and end dates.
units.context: Calendar > Recurrence > Custom recurrence using a subset of RRULE

units.source: If the recurrence string is not valid, a toast will be shown with the note ID and title of the note with the erroneous recurrence message. This note will not be added to the calendar
units.context: Calendar > Recurrence > Custom recurrence using a subset of RRULE

units.context: Calendar > Recurrence > Hiding routine events

units.source: Customizing the slot duration and label interval__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: Time slots in day and week views can be customized from __TRILIUM_PH_0__Collection Properties__TRILIUM_PH_1__
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Slot duration__TRILIUM_PH_1__ controls how tall each time slot is on the calendar (essentially the smallest unit of time the grid is divided into).
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: A shorter duration means more rows and finer granularity; a longer one means fewer, chunkier rows.
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: The default is one row every 15 minutes.
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Label interval__TRILIUM_PH_1__ controls how often a time label appears on the left-hand axis.
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: This is independent of the slot size: you can have very small slots but only label every hour to keep the axis readable.
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: The default is a time label shown every hour.
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: These values can also be customized directly via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__labels__TRILIUM_PH_3__. Both values use __TRILIUM_PH_4__ format. Hours can go up to __TRILIUM_PH_5__ (__TRILIUM_PH_6__), while minutes and seconds must be between __TRILIUM_PH_7__ and __TRILIUM_PH_8__. The minimum meaningful duration is 1 minute (__TRILIUM_PH_9__).
units.context: Calendar > Customizing the slot duration and label interval

units.source: Using with the Journal / calendar__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: It is possible to integrate the calendar view into the Journal with day notes. In order to do so change the note type of the Journal note (calendar root) to Collection and then select the Calendar View.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: While in journal mode, the popup editor will not show dates, recurrence, colors or removal, since day notes aren't editable events.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: Based on the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ (or __TRILIUM_PH_1__) attribute, the calendar will know that it's in a calendar and apply the following:
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: The calendar events are now rendered based on their __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute rather than __TRILIUM_PH_1__.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: Interactive editing such as dragging over an empty era or resizing an event is no longer possible.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: Clicking on the empty space on a date will automatically open that day's note or create it if it does not exist.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: Direct children of a day note will be displayed on the calendar despite not having a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ attribute. Children of the child notes will not be displayed.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using with the Journal / calendar

units.source: Using a different attribute as event title__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a different attribute as event title

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__By default, events are displayed on the calendar by their note title. However, it is possible to configure a different attribute to be displayed instead.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a different attribute as event title

units.source: To do so, assign __TRILIUM_PH_0__ to the child note (not the calendar/Collection note), with the value being __TRILIUM_PH_1__ where __TRILIUM_PH_2__ can be any label (make not to add the __TRILIUM_PH_3__ prefix). The attribute can also come through inheritance such as a template attribute. If the note does not have the requested label, the title of the note will be used instead.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a different attribute as event title

units.source: Using a relation attribute as event title__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a relation attribute as event title

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Similarly to using an attribute, use __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and set it to __TRILIUM_PH_2__ where __TRILIUM_PH_3__ is the name of the relation to use.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a relation attribute as event title

units.source: Moreover, if there are more relations of the same name, they will be displayed as multiple events coming from the same note.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a relation attribute as event title

units.source: __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note that it's even possible to have a __TRILIUM_PH_1__ on the target note (e.g. “John Smith”) which will try to render an attribute of it. Note that it's not possible to use a relation here as well for safety reasons (an accidental recursion  of attributes could cause the application to loop infinitely).
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Using a relation attribute as event title

units.source: Displaying an age on a recurring event__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: A birthday or an anniversary repeats every year, and what is interesting about each occurrence is the number of years it marks. To display it:
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: Set the event's start date to the original date (for example, the date of birth).
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: Click the event, then select the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Repeats__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dropdown.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: Select __TRILIUM_PH_0__Yearly__TRILIUM_PH_1__ and check __TRILIUM_PH_2__Show the number of years in the title__TRILIUM_PH_3__.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The event is then displayed as “John Smith (35)” in 2025, “John Smith (36)” in 2026, and so on. Only the calendar is affected; the note keeps its own title.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The checkbox sets the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label, which sets the title an event is displayed with and is filled in again for every occurrence the recurrence rule produces:
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: To word the title differently, edit the label directly. The checkbox is then disabled, as it is when the template is inherited, so that it never overwrites a template of your own.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The following values can be used in the template:
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: Value
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The title the event would otherwise be displayed with: the note title, or the attribute __TRILIUM_PH_0__ points to.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The whole years between __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and the occurrence being displayed. It is __TRILIUM_PH_1__ on the first occurrence.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The date of the occurrence being displayed, as a __TRILIUM_PH_0__day.js__TRILIUM_PH_1__ object. For example, __TRILIUM_PH_2__.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: The date the event starts on, in the same form. For example, __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event

units.source: To use the same template for every event of a calendar, make the label inheritable on the Collection note:
units.context: Calendar > Use-cases > Displaying an age on a recurring event
